task_description: Analyze Corey's 90-day SAGE & WEAVER launch plan for execution feasibility during holiday season

analysis_components: Capacity reality check (24h vs 320h gap identified)
Holiday impact modeling (4.0 effective working days)
Delegation potential analysis (17h freed for Greg)
Day 1 and Monday Dec 23 specific action plans

key_insights: Plan assumes 13X MORE capacity than reality (320h vs 24h)
Corporate buyers offline Dec 20 - Jan 5 (holiday timing critical)
Week 1-2 should be infrastructure build, NOT sales sprint
Delegation to Sage frees 17 hours for Greg's high-value work
Family time is infrastructure, not obstacle (sustainable > sprint)
Phase 1 should extend to 3 weeks (ends Jan 9, not Jan 2)
recommendations_made: Extend Phase 1 from 2 weeks to 3 weeks
Week 1-2 focus: Infrastructure + family time (not revenue)
Week 3 focus: Full sales activation (when buyers return)
Delegate 17 hours of automation work to Sage immediately
Monday Dec 23: 2 hours only (script, approvals, warm outreach prep)

high_risks_identified: Warm outreach gets zero response during holidays
Sales script feels awkward in real calls
mitigation_strategies: Build family time into schedule explicitly
Set expectations: warm outreach deferred to Dec 27+
Iterate script fast, record learnings from calls
Greg must provide voice/examples for Sage's templates

lessons_for_future: Capacity modeling must account for human constraints (family, energy, focus)
Corporate B2B buying cycles pause Dec 20 - Jan 5 (plan around it)
Infrastructure weeks enable velocity weeks (foundation before speed)
Delegation is force multiplier when capacity is constraint
Realistic expectations prevent burnout and disappointment

communication_approach.tone: Respectful but direct (honor Corey's vision while adjusting tactics)
communication_approach.style: Data-driven (capacity modeling, dependency mapping, risk assessment)

strengths: Grounded in calendar reality (not theoretical capacity)
Specific action plans (Day 1, Monday Dec 23, Week 1)
Clear delegation protocol (Greg vs Sage responsibilities)
areas_for_improvement: Could have included more cold email sequence examples
Could have mapped out Week 2-3 tasks in same detail as Week 1
Could have provided CRM configuration specifics
self_assessment.reasoning: Analysis grounded in verifiable constraints (holidays, human capacity, market dynamics). Recommendations are conservative but achievable.

follow_up_needed: Week 2-3 detailed task lists (if Greg requests)
Delegation protocol documentation (Greg vs Sage responsibilities)

reputation_impact.justification: Prevented unrealistic expectations, protected Greg's family time, provided actionable roadmap
